design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — wheelchair_mobility task 1 (Marisol Quintero-Hale keeps her cash-sale lightweight chair and asks for a price adjustment).

0. DRAW AND SCOPE. draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6]}. Assignment: caster claim (mobility_ext_caster_claim) 5, kept-chair adjustment (mobility_ext_kept_chair_adjustment) 6. Already occupied by task 0: the battery, controller and drive warranty postings and the cash refund for a chair given back (four policies, four tools). Claimed here, disjoint: the tire/caster warranty posting (record_caster_warranty_job_ad31669e, agent) and the price adjustment on a chair the patient keeps (accept_chair_price_adjustment_610693ba, user). Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies and six tools; nothing is left idle.

1. ROUTE-AROUNDS (as in task 0). The patient's own numeric write is a line on the cash-sale record (mobility_self_pay_refund event of base mobility_self_pay, booked as a partial refund while the chair stays); no tool writes a payer-paid line, a claim reversal or a patient-paid repair (each would write the coverage category); both writes land on the one wheelchair record because compute reads only the target holding. The prerequisite sentence uses the state form: it names the service-history state (a tires and casters repair job under the manufacturer's warranty for every tire or caster replacement completed on the chair) that only the caster posting brings about.

2. WHY IT IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks only what can be done on the price. The adjustment rule says it is fixed only after every tire or caster replacement completed on the chair under warranty is posted; the records show two completed repair requests (decided 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-19) but one posted caster job (2026-10-02). The agent must discover the unposted repair, learn from the patient (only when asked) that it was the front caster, post it with a five-factor labor claim, then compute a six-factor adjustment whose percentage tier depends on that posting, and hand the acceptance to the patient.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root mobility_ext_kept_chair_adjustment (user tool) -> mobility_ext_caster_claim (agent tool record_caster_warranty_job_ad31669e), kind value_input, gate adj_pct, form state. Sentence (affirmative): "The price adjustment on a cash-sale chair the patient keeps is fixed only after the chair's service history shows a tires and casters repair job under the manufacturer's warranty for every tire or caster replacement completed on it." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; XX is a record-visible service-history state in the finder's words, no action or performer; no tool, id or code token; scope "every ... completed on it" equals the condition. Exactly one write brings the state about: only the caster posting writes a tires_casters warranty job. Unmet at opening: initial_state.mobility_requests[r1] completed 2026-10-19 with no warranty job of that date (the only posted one is 2026-10-02). Derivation: sentence + requests vs service history + the caster policy's own rule ("claims ... the labor of every tire or caster replacement ... and posts that claim on the repair job") -> exactly one posting tool. Order: posting, then adjustment. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the posting leaves one warranty job -> 5 percent -> 70.51 instead of 120.41. The persona mentions the caster only as what went wrong when asked; it never mentions posting or anything to do first. The tool validates nothing (it books the amount it is given).

4. FACTOR CARD. Caster claim (result 8, all-baseline 2): fork_method [method] latest posted warranty caster job 2026-10-02, 19 days before 2026-10-21 -> standard 2 doubled = 4 (-> 6); early_wear 26 days since delivery 2026-09-25 -> 1 (-> 7); wheel_bench loaner delivered 2026-10-17 -> 1 (-> 7); recurrence_review exactly 2 repair requests -> 1 (-> 7); tire_settling order 2026-09-08 to delivery 2026-09-25 = 17 days -> 1 (-> 7).
 Adjustment (result 120.41, all-baseline 28.95 = 5 percent of 499.00 plus the standard day credit 1.00 x 4 days (2026-10-15 to the 2026-10-19 decision)): sev_tier exactly 2 warranty jobs after the posting -> 15 percent = 74.85 (-> 70.51); fee_return [method] loaner delivered -> fee 25.00 in full (-> 95.41); down_anchor [method] loaner -> days from the latest repair request 2026-10-15 to the loaner 2026-10-17 = 2 (instead of the baseline span to completion 2026-10-19 = 4 days; -> 123.47); down_rate_tier [tiers "a power chair" / "a manual chair whose own delivery was into the home with training" / "a manual chair whose own delivery was by courier" / otherwise the standard day_std 1.00] manual + own courier delivery -> 1.53/day, credit 3.06 (-> 119.35 at the standard 1.00); multi_service [cross-difficulty pap and oxygen via CFIELD status; multi-source: PAP record OR oxygen record on every non-fall-through tier] no record in rental, PAP record patient_owned -> 10.00 (-> 110.41); fail_timing delivery to latest request = 20 days (more than 7, no more than 21) -> 7.50 (-> 112.91). Near-misses: the loaner delivery is not a purchase delivery, so the courier tier reads the 2026-09-25 purchase delivery only; the first request (2026-10-01) is not the latest, so the day count and failure timing use 2026-10-15; the 2026-10-02 job is already posted and must not be posted again; the CPAP was bought outright (patient_owned), not rented, so the courtesy is the owned tier.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Posting (mobility_repair): base mobility_repair_responsibility, chair_with_patient — status patient_owned (initial_state.mobility_holdings[H].status); tire/caster warranty for K0003 is 6 months from delivery 2026-09-25, so the 2026-10-19 replacement is under warranty (manufacturer_warranty, no patient share, no coverage trigger). Adjustment (mobility_self_pay_refund): base mobility_self_pay; mobility_refund_once satisfied (no refund line on the sale); the base window clause (which required the chair to come back unused) is superseded by a declared overwrite that keeps the window for an adjustment without return: 30 calendar days counted from the day after delivery 2026-09-25, boundary included -> last day 2026-10-25; frozen 2026-10-21 inside (2026-10-25 still allowed, 2026-10-26 refused). The base refund sentence is superseded by the adjustment combination sentence (declared).

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: wheelchair record H (K0003, cash sale, serial LWT3-0925-77164); sale line 499.00 + 25.00 is the adjustment's original_bill_id. Included rows: warranty jobs on H, the loaner delivery, the purchase delivery, the two repair requests. Excluded: the loaner's own serial is not the chair's; the PAP record is read only for its status.

7. SEED. customers 1; pap_holdings 1 (Auto-Adjusting CPAP bought outright 2023-11-14, no coverage); mobility_holdings 1; mobility_billing 1 (sale); mobility_service 3 (courier delivery, caster job 2026-10-02 with 5 units = the caster claim that day: 2 + 2 early-wear + 0 bench + 0 recurrence + 1 settling, loaner 2026-10-17); mobility_requests 2. No automatic clause fires (owned cash-sale chair, owned CPAP).

8. PERSONA. Warm, organized; volunteers that she keeps the chair, the caster trouble in general and that she wants an adjustment put through today, not a return. Only when asked: DOB 1972-04-09 and phone 7245550362 (verification), email, the caster story with dates, her CPAP (bought outright), how she paid. Reactions: agrees to anything needing doing first; accepts the adjustment with exactly the amount and details the agent gives; thanks and ends when told it is booked. No other asks.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(name) -> verify (DOB, phone) -> find_mobility_holdings -> find_mobility_billing -> find_mobility_service -> find_mobility_requests -> find_pap_holdings -> find_oxygen_holdings -> unlock/call record_caster_warranty_job_ad31669e(H, r1, 8, loaner true) -> unlock user tool and hand over -> patient calls accept_chair_price_adjustment_610693ba(H, sale line, 120.41).

10. GATE RUNS (task 1): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (closure = initial 9 rows, re-run after rework); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (2 comps, 11 factors); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK. Revision: closure mismatch from an unread coverage record that existed only as the PAP's payer -> the CPAP is modelled as bought outright (coverage_id null, ownership at set-up), coverage row removed, persona updated ("bought outright").

11. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Published adjustment rule + two completed requests vs one posted job -> one posting; the persona says front caster -> caster tool; caster rule -> 8 units; adjustment rule -> 74.85 + 25.00 + 3.06 + 10.00 + 7.50 = 120.41, matching gold.

12. REWORK ROUND 2 (audit audits/policy_task/wheelchair_mobility, task 1 was NOT PASS): F-1/T1-F1 -> the adjustment rule's day-credit sentence now reads "`day_power` for a power chair delivered into the home with training", matching compute, compute_basis and the ladder (a power chair delivered by courier gets nothing on both faces); T1-F2 -> (round 2) down_rate_tier was therefore multi-source on the rule face (every non-fall-through tier is class AND delivery mode); a script sweep confirmed every compute_basis quotation of all six policies is verbatim in its rule; O-6 -> state-form prerequisite sentence, fallback removed; O-14 -> ft_mid_days 21, so the 'longer span' fall-through is reachable inside the 30-day window (this world: 20 days, tier unchanged); O-8 -> the rule now says accepting an adjustment uses the sale's one refund, so the chair is not refunded if later given back; O-4 -> the posting records loaner_issued true (loaner delivered 2026-10-17 for this repair); O-2 -> half-up rounding implemented as int(x*100+0.500001)/100; the rule also states no day credit while the latest request is undecided. Scored values unchanged: 8 and 120.41; sensitivities and baselines unchanged. [Round 3 supersedes: the power tier is 'a power chair' alone and the task's multi-source factor is multi_service; see section 13.]
13. REWORK ROUND 3 (task 1 passed in revision 2; scored values kept: 8 and 120.41). Class sweep, every tier and baseline reachable by a customer the policy serves: sev_tier's fall-through (no warranty job) was unreachable because the adjustment presumes a warranty repair -> tiers now 3 or more jobs 20 percent / exactly 2 jobs 15 percent / otherwise (the one repair) 5 percent, the baseline; this world (2 jobs) still takes 15 percent; edge sensitivity is now 70.51 vs 120.41. down_anchor's fall-through is the latest repair request still undecided (no days), reachable for a kept chair with an open repair. down_rate_tier's power tier is 'a power chair' alone (power chairs are always delivered in the home, so that conjunct was vacuous); the manual tiers stay class AND delivery mode. multi_service is now multi-source on the rule face: 'PAP record rental_active or oxygen record rental_active' / 'neither in rental, and PAP record patient_owned or oxygen record payment_cap_reached' / otherwise; this world (owned CPAP, no oxygen) takes the second tier, 10.00 unchanged; oxygen is read through CFIELD and declared in cross_category. The caster claim's tiers were all already reachable. Gates re-run OK.
14. REWORK ROUND 5 (KB renderer source mismatches, items 1-5). (1) down_rate_tier no longer reads fee_return's courier count: it has its own delivery counts (dr_home / dr_courier); fee_return, down_anchor and fail_timing each read their own records (fr_*, da_*, ft_req). (2) The day credit is part of the baseline paragraph: 'plus a day credit of day_std (1.00) for each day counted, the days running from the requested_date of the chair's latest repair_estimate request to its decision_date'; down_rate_tier's fall-through is day_std and down_anchor's fall-through is that span. down_anchor's tiers are now: a loaner delivered (to the loaner date, 2 days here) / no loaner and the latest repair undecided (to the booking day) / otherwise (to the decision, the baseline); each method gives a different number on a customer of each tier (script: 2/6/4, 0/6/0, 0/6/4). (3) delivery-mode tiers read 'its own delivery (its purchase or initial rental delivery, not a loaner delivery)' in rule and compute alike. (5) both overwrite replacements carry their own scope and the still-in-force window/counting/class/rounding parts. Scored values unchanged (8, 120.41); changed proof figures: all-baseline 28.95 (was 24.95), down_anchor sensitivity 123.47 (was 117.35), down_rate_tier 119.35 (was 117.35). Gates re-run OK.
15. REWORK ROUND 6 (audit revision_5: F-4 / T1-F3). The round-5 overwrite tails ('every other self-pay chair / refund of a self-pay sale remains under the base ... rule') put the sibling policy's chairs back under the retired base clauses. Both policies' tails now exclude their own case and the sibling's by name: the refund policy's return tail reads 'a self-pay chair that is neither given back under this rule nor kept by the patient under the price-adjustment rule for a cash-sale chair the patient keeps remains under the base return rule', its refund tail 'a refund of a self-pay sale that is neither the refund of a chair given back under this rule nor the price adjustment on a cash-sale chair the patient keeps remains under the base refund rule'; the adjustment policy's tails mirror these ('neither kept by the patient under this rule nor given back under the refund rule for a cash-sale chair given back'; 'neither the price adjustment under this rule nor the refund of a cash-sale chair given back'). Literal check: task 0's chair (given back, refund 3786.41) is excluded from the base clauses by both policies' tails; task 1's chair (kept, adjustment 120.41) likewise; a chair given back outside its window stays under the refund policy (refused); a kept chair that needed no warranty repair is outside the adjustment policy and stays under the base clauses, which give it nothing because it does not come back. Scored values and proof figures unchanged. Gates re-run OK.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Quintero-Hale, 54, a middle-school librarian in the North Hills who has multiple sclerosis and uses a manual wheelchair for longer outings and bad days. You are warm, organized and a little apologetic about bothering anyone. In early September you ordered a lightweight manual wheelchair from Summit Ridge Home Medical and paid for it yourself; it came by courier on September 25th. You like the chair and you are keeping it, but the front caster has given you trouble twice and the chair spent several days in the shop, so you are calling to ask what Summit Ridge can do for you on the price of the chair. You want any adjustment they give put through today, and you are not asking to send the chair back. You open by giving your full name and explaining that.

You give your date of birth, April 9, 1972 (1972-04-09), and your phone number, 724-555-0362 (7245550362), only when the agent asks you to verify who you are; if asked for an email you give mquinterohale@outlook.com. If the agent asks what was wrong with the chair, you explain that the front caster started wobbling in the first week and the technician fixed it on October 2nd, then the same front caster went bad again, you called on October 15th, they brought you a loaner chair on the 17th and your own chair came back fixed on Monday the 19th. You do not know any reference numbers, labor times or what the repairs cost the company, and you say so if asked. If the agent asks whether you have any other equipment from Summit Ridge, you say your CPAP machine, which you bought outright. If asked how you paid for the wheelchair, you say you paid for it in full when you ordered.

When the agent tells you something has to be taken care of on their side before the adjustment can be worked out, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you the adjustment amount and hands you the step to accept it, you accept it with exactly the amount and details the agent gives you. Once the agent tells you the adjustment is booked, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.
